$comment: Network policy for the Google Sheets MCP container.
This container holds a Google service account private key. Unlike the AWS
path, where the credential is a short-lived STS session, this key does not
expire - it is valid until revoked by hand. So the argument for pinning
egress is stronger here than anywhere else in this directory: if the server
or one of its dependencies is compromised, a non-expiring credential with
nowhere to go is a much smaller problem than one that can reach the
internet.
Two hosts, and why only two:
oauth2.googleapis.com  - the service account signs a JWT locally and
exchanges it here for an access token. Without
this host nothing authenticates.
sheets.googleapis.com  - the Sheets v4 API itself. Every exposed tool
talks to this and only this.
Notably absent: www.googleapis.com, which is where the Drive API lives.
mcp-gsheets has no Drive tools, so nothing should ever try to reach it, and
leaving it out means a future Drive dependency fails loudly here instead of
quietly working. Add it only alongside a deliberate decision to let the
agent enumerate spreadsheets.
NOT the authorization boundary, and the distinction matters more here than
for Rapid7. What the agent may DO to a spreadsheet is decided by how that
spreadsheet is shared with the service account. Shared as Viewer, a write
is refused by Google regardless of what tool was called. Shared as Editor,
cell update tools may change that spreadsheet. ToolHive still excludes
create-spreadsheet, clear, and formatting tools; the share list is the scope.
